subject: Anchoring configuration recommendations + A/B plan for Delta Health
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Alvarez <s.alvarez@deltahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap — anchoring config & next steps

Hi Sofia — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and recommended starting point for the evaluation sandbox so your team can reproduce the benchmarks we discussed. I captured the items we agreed on plus a proposed A/B plan.

Recap / recommended baseline:
- Model variants to test (both served from Redwood Dedicated):
  * Variant A: redwood-13b-v2 (int8/quantized) — balances cost and generation quality for clinical prose.
  * Variant B: redwood-30b-mm (fp16) — higher quality on complex references, useful for higher-sensitivity flows.
- Retrieval config (initial):
  * Chunk size: 450–600 tokens (start at 500)
  * Overlap: 50 tokens
  * Top-k candidate fetch: 12
  * Reranker candidates: 6 (rerank top 6 with cross-encoder)
- Embedding model: text-embedding-3-small (consistent with your current index)
- Vector store: FAISS flat for the pilot (we can move to HNSW for scale)
- Reranker options to compare in A/B:
  * Option 1 (A): cross-encoder re-ranker (mT5-cross-encoder-v2) — higher precision, heavier latency.
  * Option 2 (B): lightweight dense-sim dot-product reranker (sparse-rerank-v1) — lower latency, slightly lower precision.

Benchmarks we think are relevant to capture: grounding rate (precision@1 on annotated queries), hallucination rate (manual error rate on 200-sample probe), latency p95 generation + rerank, and cost per 1k queries. I've uploaded an initial prompt suite and the short benchmark harness.

Ask / next steps:
1) Can you confirm access for our evaluation runner to the Delta eval index (read-only)? Ideally a temp API key for the sandbox environment by Monday.
2) We propose an A/B run: Variant A (cross-encoder rerank) vs Variant B (dot-product rerank) across the same 1,500 prompts. Plan: 72-hour steady-state run, collect grounding + latencies + qualitative failures.
3) Please review the attached prompt set (delta_eval_promptset_v1.csv) and flag any PHI-sensitive items you want removed.

Links / attachments:
- Attachment: delta_eval_promptset_v1.csv (prompt set + labels)
- Attachment: anchor_metrics_snapshot_20270514.png (sample expected metrics)
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1X-example-benchmark-results (starter benchmark harness)

If that looks good I can schedule the A/B run and loop in Ops to provision the dedicated nodes. Thanks — happy to jump on a short follow-up if you'd like to walk through the experiment design.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Alvarez <s.alvarez@deltahealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Delta Health evaluation team <eval@deltahealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — anchoring config & next steps

Thanks Jasmine — this is very clear and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick asks from our side: 

- We can provide a read-only key scoped to the evaluation index; I'll have our infra team generate it by Monday morning (PST).
- For the A/B plan, can you confirm what the expected incremental cost delta would be between the cross-encoder rerank and the dot-product rerank at ~5k queries/day? We need that for procurement.
- We also want to include a small cohort of patient-scenario prompts that contain redacted PHI to validate no leakage in retrieval. We'll add those to your prompt set (you mentioned you can scrub on your side if needed).

Quick confirmation: we want the A/B to report the following metrics out-of-the-box: grounding precision@1, hallucination manual rate (sampled 200), p95 latency, and per-query cost. If you can add a small column to the harness to tag the prompt sensitivity level (low/med/high) that would be helpful.

Sofia
Sofia Alvarez
Director, Applied AI
Delta Health

LGTM. A couple technical notes before we kick the run: 

- For clinical Qs, bump the effective retrieval window to 3 documents in the rerank candidate set (keeps precision high on multi-sentence answers).
- Turn off prefix KV caching for flows that touch patient identifiers — avoids accidental reuse across sessions.
- Reranker perf: expect +30–50ms p95 for cross-encoder on 6 candidates on a V100-class node; plan capacity accordingly. If Delta wants lower latency we can shard reranker across two smaller instances and aggregate.
- Cost estimate (very rough): cross-encoder rerank increases per-query CPU cost by ~2.5x vs dot-product (networking + cross-encoder compute). We'll draft a tighter estimate after we get the exact query mix from Sofia.

I'll prepare a pointer config for Ops with the above values (chunk 500 / overlap 50 / top-k 12 / rerank 6 / retrieve-window 3) and drop it in the Drive link Jasmine shared. Once the read-only key is live we can start the 72-hr A/B.

—Marcus
Staff ML Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
